item.text: {"text":"KERPLE (Chi et al., NeurIPS 2022) is direct prior art for the attention bias b(i,j)=−r₁ log(1+r₂|i−j|), with positive, learned head-specific parameters. The formula itself is established; applying it to bidirectional BERT4Rec is an adaptation. Compared with ALiBi’s fixed linear distance penalty, KERPLE learns logarithmic decay. T5 instead learns bucket values with logarithmic distance bucketing, allowing nonmonotonic biases; KERPLE’s positive logarithmic form remains monotonic. The original evidence concerns language-model length extrapolation, not recommendation accuracy. [Paper](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=hXzOqPlXDwm)\n\nThe reference implementation initializes r₁ uniformly in [0,2) and r₂ uniformly in [0,1), then clamps both to at least 0.01. Its distance matrix is lower triangular for causal attention; bidirectional use requires the full absolute-distance matrix and a separate padding mask. Direct differentiation gives ∂b/∂r₁=−log(1+r₂d) and ∂b/∂r₂=−r₁d/(1+r₂d). Thus, initializing both effective parameters to zero makes both derivatives zero; initializing only one to zero can let the other receive a gradient. Tiny positive values can weaken learning, while softplus parameters initialized far below zero add further gradient attenuation. Moderate positive effective initialization permits nonzero local gradients for d>0, although actual learning still depends on attention and loss gradients. These gradient conclusions are mathematical deductions; no proposed initialization values were supplied to assess specifically. [Reference implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chijames/KERPLE/main/megatron/mpu/layers.py)"}
